chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Paris 1947: French jazz fans booing bebop
summary: On the 1947 trip with Slam Stewart, Hawkins and Howard McGhee, Hugues Panassie's seat block booed the bebop group at the Marini Theatre.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I don't know whether I mentioned this before, but my first trip to Europe, which was 1947, I went over with Slam Stewart, Errol Garner, and myself. This was a trio. It was -- I've seen it listed in some -- as some jazz critic is writing history of jazz, said it was Errol Garner's trio. It was not Errol Garner's trio, it was Slam Stewart's trio. Okay. So it was -- Howard McGhee had the band, and --

He had a band. Okay, it was Errol Garner, myself and Slam. Slam Stewart Trio. Howard McGhee's band and Coleman Hawkins, it was his first time in Europe since the war, you know. He left because of the war, and this was his first trip, which was like a triumphal return, you know. And I know I mentioned that the singer there was Chippy Hill. She was a blues singer. Yeah. But the one thing that I remembered about that trip was how fanatical the French people were about jazz. Traditional jazz as opposed to bop.

Now, as you know Howard McGhee was a bebop. This is the bebop era. Of course our group spanned both eras, and so did Coleman Hawkins, but the main bone of contention was Howard McGhee's group, and we played at the Marini Theatre, it's right at the foot of the Champs Elysees. And Panassie had bought a block of seats and they came there to boo, and they would boo, you know. They actually came -- every concert they were there and they would whistle, boo, you know, because
of the bebop. And so I had another experience like that.
